framework: Behavioral Economics
---

# Pricing sensitivity by segment

A round of casual pricing conversations with existing customers surfaced a pattern the sales lead had not expected: the pharmacy contracts, which carry the strictest temperature tolerance and the most regulatory consequence for a failure, are also the least price-sensitive of the three segments, while the dairy subscriptions, which carry the loosest tolerance and the least consequence for a minor breach, are the most price-sensitive by a wide margin.

The read the sales lead has settled on, provisionally, is that customers are not really pricing the delivery itself, they are pricing the cost of what happens if the cold chain fails, and that cost differs enormously by what is inside the box: a spoiled dairy subscription is an annoyed customer and a refund, a spoiled pharmaceutical shipment can be a regulatory incident. If that read holds, it suggests any new segment should be priced against the downside of a failure for that specific segment, not against a flat per-delivery rate copied from the existing business.
